newsitem.title: IRAQ: Baghdad says to complete pullout from n.Iraq today.
newsitem.headline: Baghdad says to complete pullout from n.Iraq today.

text.p: Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz said Baghdad would complete a troop withdrawal from Kurdish north on Tuesday and denied reports that Iraq was massing forces close to the town of Sulaimaniya.

"Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz ridiculed American claims on Iraqi troop movements towards Sulaimaniya," the official Iraqi News Agency (INA) said. "Our troops have started withdrawing to former positions and will complete their return today," INA quoted Aziz as saying.

Iraqi forces on Saturday seized the Kurdish city of Arbil from the rebel Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) after a rival group, the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), asked for Baghdad's help against the PUK.
The United States reacted by firing 27 cruise missiles at what it said were military targets in southern Iraq on Tuesday.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said on Monday there was evidence that some of the Iraqi forces were penetrating deeper into Kurdish-populated areas and were threatening Sulaymania, a PUK-controlled town close to the Iranian border.
